questions.question: What happens if air pressure is lost in the emergency line?

options.text: The suspension springs extend.
The tractor protection valve opens.
The rear trailer detaches.
The emergency brakes activate.

questions.explanation: The emergency air line controls the emergency brakes. If air pressure is lost in this line, the emergency trailer brakes will activate right away.

questions.question: What does an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) do?

options.text: Allows wheels to lock up.
Stops wheels from locking up.
Makes it easier to turn a large vehicle.
Helps brake lights work.

questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) prevents your wheels from locking up when you brake hard.

questions.question: When coupling a trailer, what should you do with the glad hands?

options.text: Connect matching glad hands together.
You can connect any glad hand to any other glad hand.
Leave one glad hand unattached.
Connect only one set of glad hands.

questions.explanation: Connect matching glad hands together. They are often color-coded to help you avoid mistakes. Blue is usually for service lines and red is for emergency lines.

questions.question: When does an automatic tractor protection valve pop out?

options.text: When air pressure drops to between 20 and 45 psi.
When the trailer jackknifes.
When wheels regain traction after a skid.
When air pressure is above 45 psi.

questions.correctAnswerText: When air pressure drops to between 20 and 45 psi.
questions.explanation: An automatic tractor protection valve pops out when air pressure drops to between 20 and 45 psi. When it pops out, the valve closes and stops air flow.

questions.question: What problem can result from not greasing the fifth wheel plate?

options.text: The trailer may disconnect.
Steering problems may occur.
Braking problems may occur.
The lights may not work.

questions.explanation: If the fifth wheel plate is not properly greased, friction between the tractor and trailer increases, which causes steering problems.

questions.question: How do fully-loaded rigs compare to empty rigs regarding rollover risk?

options.text: They are less likely to roll over.
They are more likely to roll over.
They have the same rollover risk.
They should never be driven.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are more likely to roll over.
questions.explanation: Fully-loaded rigs have a higher center of gravity because of the cargo weight. This makes them 10 times more likely to roll over in a crash than empty rigs.

questions.question: Where can trailers with low underneath clearance be difficult to drive?

options.text: On interstate highways.
Over railroad crossings.
On dirt roads.
At the posted speed limit.

questions.explanation: Trailers with low underneath clearance are difficult to drive over railroad-highway crossings. This is especially true for low-slung units and single-axle tractors pulling long trailers.

questions.question: How do you test the trailer service brakes?

options.text: Move forward slowly and press the brake pedal.
Reverse slowly and use the hand control to brake.
Reverse slowly and press the brake pedal.
Move forward slowly and use the hand control to brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move forward slowly and use the hand control to brake.
questions.explanation: To test the trailer service brakes, first check that the air pressure is normal and release the parking brake. Then move forward slowly and use the hand control to brake. If the brakes work properly, you will feel them activate.

questions.question: What is the best way to notice that your trailer is starting to skid?

options.text: By looking at other drivers' faces.
By looking in your mirrors.
By feeling it.
By listening to the radio.

questions.explanation: The earliest and best way to notice a trailer skid is to see the trailer moving off course in your mirrors.

questions.question: Why do combination vehicles need more road space than other commercial vehicles?

options.text: They need more space to turn and stop.
They drive more slowly.
They are twice as wide.
They swerve more often.

questions.correctAnswerText: They need more space to turn and stop.
questions.explanation: Because combination vehicles are longer, they need more space to turn and stop. Managing space properly is important when you drive a combination vehicle.

questions.question: Rollovers happen when:

options.text: A truck driver is driving too fast.
The driver in front of a truck is moving too slowly.
A truck driver is driving too slowly.
ABS is working properly.

questions.correctAnswerText: A truck driver is driving too fast.
questions.explanation: Rollovers happen when a vehicle is driven too fast. To lower the risk of rollover, load cargo weight low to the ground. Also, take turns and curves slowly.

questions.question: One function of the emergency air line is to:

options.text: Control the emergency brakes.
Flash when air pressure drops below a certain level.
Allow for quick turning.
Control how well the vehicle handles in bad weather.

questions.explanation: The emergency air line (also called the supply line) has two functions. It supplies air to the trailer air tanks. It also controls the emergency brakes on combination vehicles.

questions.question: The trailer hand valve:

options.text: Should always be used for parking.
Should only be used for parking on a downhill.
Should never be used for parking.
Should only be used when carrying cargo.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should never be used for parking.
questions.explanation: Never use the trailer hand valve for parking. This can let all air out of the brake system, which causes the brakes to release. Use the parking brake instead.

questions.question: Trailers made after ____ must have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS).
questions.explanation: Trailers and converter dollies made on or after March 1, 1998 must have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS).

questions.question: When a combination vehicle goes around a corner:

options.text: The turn should be as tight as possible.
The front and rear wheels follow different paths.
The rear wheels should run over the curb.
It is okay to knock over street signs if they are too close to the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front and rear wheels follow different paths.
questions.explanation: When a vehicle turns a corner, the rear wheels follow a different path than the front wheels. This is called off-tracking. This effect is even more pronounced on vehicles with trailers.

questions.question: When backing a trailer, which way should you turn the steering wheel?

options.text: Turn the steering wheel in the direction you want the trailer to go.
Turn the steering wheel in the opposite direction of where you want the trailer to go.
It doesn't matter.
It depends on where you are backing the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the steering wheel in the opposite direction of where you want the trailer to go.
questions.explanation: When backing with a trailer, turn the steering wheel in the opposite direction of where you want to go. Once the trailer starts turning, switch the steering wheel direction to follow the trailer.

questions.question: When connecting a converter dolly to a second or third trailer, the trailer height should be:

options.text: Slightly higher than the center of the fifth wheel.
Level with the center of the fifth wheel.
Slightly lower than the center of the fifth wheel.
Next to the center of the fifth wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slightly lower than the center of the fifth wheel.
questions.explanation: When connecting a converter dolly to a second or third trailer, the trailer height should be slightly lower than the center of the fifth wheel.

questions.question: If the emergency line loses air pressure, it will:

options.text: Activate the service brakes.
Close the tractor protection valve.
Cause the rear trailer to detach from the combination.
Extend the suspension springs.

questions.explanation: The tractor protection valve keeps air in the trailer's brake system if the trailer breaks away or develops a leak. A loss of air pressure in the emergency line will close the tractor protection valve and activate the emergency trailer brakes.

questions.question: Simply changing lanes can cause:

options.text: A "crack-the-whip" effect that can cause a rollover.
A trailer to straighten out.
Confusion about which lane the driver wants to use.
Other drivers to slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: A "crack-the-whip" effect that can cause a rollover.
questions.explanation: Because of the "crack-the-whip" effect from rearward amplification, changing lanes too quickly in a combination vehicle can cause a rollover.

questions.question: A shut-off valve:

options.text: Is located on the front of a trailer.
Is located on the instrument panel.
Stops air from escaping the air brake system.
Should always be open.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stops air from escaping the air brake system.
questions.explanation: Shut-off valves control air flow through supply lines from one trailer to another. The rear shut-off valve should always be closed to prevent air from leaving the brake system.
